I'm reviewing a list of security issues found in the codebase, starting with several problems in the SSO group mapping service around arbitrary org-role updates, non-transactional role syncing, and incomplete cleanup during demotions, plus an auth config route vulnerability where project admins can access other users' OIDC claims.

Continuing through the remaining issues: there's a problem in the tRPC layer where role editing becomes unavailable when OIDC group mapping is configured but OIDC itself is misconfigured, several UI issues in the auth form around social sign-in persistence and flash states, a stale user ID reference in the SSO token inspector after project changes, and blocking login behavior from synchronous role syncing. There's also an issue where non-OIDC logins reapply stale OIDC group memberships, and a hook that defaults to false while loading.

The user wants me to focus only on fixes that make practical sense, report each error individually, and delegate each fix to a subagent using the gpt-5.6-sol-high-fast model. I need to first check whether the branch is already checked out locally.…
I found 13 issues across 8 files in the review document. I'm checking the local repo state to understand what changes have been made since the PR was pushed, since git status shows uncommitted changes on several of those same files.

content.text:
The local branch has an unpushed commit (544f52b9) that adds SSO_SESSION_MAX_AGE, while the PR itself shows only 2 commits. The working tree is clean aside from untracked storage files—the modified files from earlier were committed as part of that new commit. Now I'm reviewing the relevant files to work through the 13 issues.…
The branch is checked out locally with one extra commit and a clean working tree. Now I'll review the touched files to triage each issue against the current code.
Now let me read the remaining files involved in the review.

I'm going through each of the 13 issues and need to understand a few key things: whether this is a single-org self-hosted setup (where `getUserOrgMembership` returns just one membership) versus the multi-org cloud scenario, and how member role editing handles context-explorer cleanup and demotion logic in the org routes. I also need to look into issue 12 regarding stale OIDC configuration.…
I've loaded the code and now I'm checking how manual role demotion handles worktree cleanup, the org membership query, and where `updateMemberRole` is located to properly triage the issues.

I'm triaging the 13 issues and starting with the backend. The first one is in the SSO group mapping service where `getUserOrgMembership` uses `.limit(1)` to return a single membership, but this reflects the app's assumption that users belong to only one organization—self-hosted instances have a default org and cloud creates personal orgs. The existing org routes also query for a single membership, so the "unrelated organizations" edge case doesn't really surface in the current data model.

For the second issue around project syncing, I'm considering whether projects can span multiple orgs for a user. Projects have an orgId and members are added within the org context, so in cloud a user could theoretically be a member of projects across different orgs. Rather than skip this entirely, a minimal scoping fix makes sense—filtering project memberships to match the resolved org membership would be cheap and reasonable. I'd join `listProjectMembershipsForUser` with `project.orgId` to scope the results.

On the transactionality concern with SSO group mapping, the count-then-demote race condition is theoretical and only occurs during concurrent SSO sign-ins of the last two admins. Since the existing manual demotion paths in the codebase follow the same non-transactional pattern without transactions, this is consistent with current behavior. Adding transactions across SQLite/Postgres would introduce unnecessary complexity for an extremely narrow failure mode, so I'll skip this one.

The worktree cleanup issue is valid though—when manually demoting someone from admin or context_admin roles, the code cleans up their context worktrees, but the SSO sync doesn't do the same. I need to add that cleanup logic after updating the project member role.

The cross-tenant token disclosure in auth-config.routes.ts is the highest priority fix—I need to verify the target user is actually a member of the current project before allowing token inspection.

For the OIDC misconfiguration issue, the problem is that `isGroupRoleMappingActive` checks if the mapping exists and the license is valid, but doesn't verify OIDC is actually configured. If an admin sets up group-role mapping without configuring OIDC, the sync never runs but manual edits get blocked. I need to add an `isOidcConfigured()` check to the condition.

On the frontend side, the remember-on-click heuristic for OAuth is acceptable as a P3 issue—it's a common pattern and the worst case is just showing the wrong provider once.

The email form flash on cold load is a real P2 UX bug: provider queries start loading, the form collapses, then expands again when queries resolve. The fix is straightforward—don't render either the providers or email form while loading to avoid the flash, then delegate the implementation.

The "Last used" pill showing for email is dead code since that condition can't actually occur.

For the "Last used" badge appearing on the forgot-password page, it's misleading since that context doesn't apply there. The AuthForm doesn't know which page it's on, but I could scope the badge to only show when it makes sense, or add a prop to control it.

Looking at the SSO token inspector issue — when the project changes, the members list updates but the selected user ID stays the same, which could point to someone no longer in the list. The fix is straightforward: if the selected user isn't in the new members list, fall back to the session user.

For the login flow concern, syncing roles from SSO groups adds a few queries during sign-in, but awaiting it ensures roles are updated before the session becomes usable — that's actually the right behavior for security, so I'd leave it as-is. The real issue is when a non-OIDC login happens after an OIDC login; the session hook reads the stored ID token from the last OIDC login and reapplies those groups even though the user might have been removed from them. les the last OIDC sign-in applied. The real issue is that when an IdP moves a user to a lower group, their roles stay elevated until they sign in via OIDC again — but if SSO_SESSION_MAX_AGE forces a re-login and they choose password instead, stale roles persist. Restricting the sync to OIDC sessions would be cleaner. To identify the provider in the session hook, I'd need to check the context — better-auth passes `ctx` to `session.create.after`, which might have path info or a `resolveProviderId` function similar to what's available in user creation hooks.

The fix would be to only sync groups when `resolveProviderId(ctx)` matches the OIDC provider ID. But this creates a tradeoff: a user whose groups changed and signs in with a password won't get synced, which is the same outcome as the current scenario. The question is whether reapplying stale OIDC data on non-OIDC logins is actually harmful — since roles can't be manually edited while mapping is active, it's idempotent, except the org routes block `updateMemberRole` anyway. There's also the edge case of a user deactivated in the IdP who can still password login.

Actually, reapplication is mostly a no-op unless roles were changed elsewhere. The real edge case is when the last-admin guard skipped a demotion earlier, then another admin gets added, and a password re-login applies that stale demotion from an old token — which could be correct or could be stale. Restricting sync to OIDC sessions feels like a legitimate small fix that also addresses the latency issue for non-SSO users. I need to check the `resolveProviderId` signature and whether the session hook receives the context.

Now looking at the false-while-loading issue in the role mapping hook — I could expose `isLoading` or handle the unloaded state differently instead of treating it as managed.…
I have a full picture now. Let me check how AuthForm is used on the forgot-password page, whether resolveProviderId can help the session hook identify the provider, and the manual role-update path in user.routes.ts.

I've triaged seven issues that need fixing. The highest priority is a cross-tenant OIDC claims disclosure vulnerability in the auth config routes—I need to validate that the target user belongs to the current project context. There's also a role editing bug where the check for active group role mapping should additionally verify OIDC is configured. A third issue involves SSO demotions skipping some workflow, though that thought cuts off.

For the remaining fixes: I need to restrict sync operations to OIDC sign-ins by checking the provider ID during session creation, which should also help with latency for non-SSO logins. The auth form has a flash issue on cold load that I can fix by deferring render until provider queries complete. Finally, there's a dead "Last used" pill in the form that I should either remove or make reachable depending on whether it makes sense in the collapsed button state.

The "Last used" indicator on forgot/reset/modify password pages is showing up when it shouldn't — it only matters when both the email form is visible and social providers are displayed. I can gate this by only setting `emailLastUsed` when `displaySocialProviders` is true, which keeps it scoped to login/signup pages. For the SSO token inspector, I need to handle stale user selections across project switches by falling back to the session user when the selection isn't in the current members list.

For the role mapping hook, I should expose the loading state and disable role editing in the dialog while data is being fetched. That brings me to nine fixes total, though some are marked as won't-fix — like the multi-org concern in the SSO group mapping service, which assumes single org membership throughout the codebase. Scoping project updates to the org membership would add robustness but requires a new query joining the project table.

The transaction race condition in the group mapping follows the same count-then-write pattern already present in the user routes, so the risk window is negligible and not worth a cross-dialect refactor. For the blocking login issue, fix B12 partially mitigates it by skipping the await for non-OIDC sign-ins, but keeping the await for OIDC flows is intentional to ensure roles stay synchronized.

The click-time recording for last-used hints is a cosmetic P3 issue — most products record on attempt rather than success, and wiring it through the OAuth callback would add unnecessary complexity. Rather than fixing each issue individually, I'm batching them into subagents using the high-speed model, grouping by file to avoid conflicts. The backend security and config fixes will go to one agent handling the auth configuration and SSO group mapping services. I'm thinking through how to organize these fixes into parallel waves to avoid file conflicts. I'll group B5 and B3 together since they both touch the same service file, then run B4, B12, and the frontend fixes in parallel waves where the files don't overlap.

I should also make sure the agents update the relevant test files when they modify behavior, and I'll use gpt-5.6-sol-high-fast as the model for these subagents.

Once they finish, I need to run the linter and backend tests, then compile the report based on any errors that come up. For the B3 fix specifically, I'm thinking through how to handle the worktree cleanup when a user's role is demoted from admin or context_admin — I'll need to either fetch the project by ID or extend the listProjectMembershipsForUser query to include the project path, and I can import cleanupContextWorktree from the context-explorer-git service.

The tricky part is avoiding circular imports since auth.ts already uses dynamic imports to prevent cycles with sso-group-mapping.service, so I should follow that same pattern here. For B5, I need to add an OIDC check to isGroupRoleMappingActive and make sure the tests get updated accordingly. For B12, the session creation hook receives the session and context, so I'll gate the logic on whether the resolved provider ID matches the OIDC provider ID, but I need to verify the exact signature in better-auth's types first.

The callback path varies depending on how the OIDC provider is registered — it could be `/callback/:id` for social providers or `/oauth2/callback/:providerId` for the generic OAuth plugin. I need to check how augmentPluginsWithOidc registers the provider to determine what the context will look like. The key is only syncing when the session creation is triggered by an actual OIDC callback request, and skipping if the context is undefined since that indicates internal session creation.

For the loading states, I'm weighing whether to defer rendering the email form until all provider queries settle. The tradeoff is between showing a brief blank space (which feels less jarring than form elements disappearing) versus the flash of loading skeletons. For deployments without social providers, hiding the email form during load then revealing it creates an awkward blank space, but that's probably preferable to form collapse and focus loss. The approach is to treat providers as unsettled while queries are pending and render a placeholder during that window, though this does add a brief delay for pure email/password setups.

I also need to check whether useIsMicrosoftSetup exposes a loading state, and I should gate the emailLastUsed pill to pages where displaySocialProviders is true—though on the login page it's fine to show even without providers configured since that's the intended use case for the pill.

For the members list, I'll use a derived value to check if the selectedUserId exists in the loaded data, falling back to the session user if it doesn't, rather than managing this with an effect. When loading the role editor, I need to disable the dropdown and prevent premature editing, then send the newRole based on the resolved value. On the backend, I should verify the target membership exists before proceeding with role changes.…
I've finished triage and now I'm checking what `project.listAllUsersWithRoles` returns to make sure the P1 fix doesn't break the token inspector's user dropdown.

The dropdown correctly scopes `inspectToken` to project members, which aligns with the UI design. I'm now triaging the remaining issues—nine fixes grouped across six subagents, starting with the cross-tenant auth vulnerability in `inspectToken`, followed by SSO group mapping dependencies and worktree cleanup logic.…
I've triaged all 13 issues and identified 9 worth fixing, organized into 6 work packages by file. Now I'll send each package to a subagent, then lint, test, and provide you with a detailed error report.

Fix a P1 security issue found in review of PR #1389, in apps/backend/src/trpc/auth-config.routes.ts around line 93-100:

The `oidc.inspectToken` procedure is an `adminProtectedProcedure` (caller must be an admin of `ctx.project`), but it forwards `input.userId` unscoped to `inspectSsoToken(input.userId ?? ctx.user.id)`. A project admin can therefore read ANY user's stored OIDC ID-token claims (including users outside their project/org) by supplying an arbitrary userId — a cross-tenant disclosure.

Fix: before calling `inspectSsoToken` with a target user other than the caller, validate that the target user is a member of `ctx.project`. Use the existing query `projectQueries.getUserRoleInProject(ctx.project.id, targetUserId)` from '../queries/project.queries' (returns the role or null). If the target has no role in the project, throw a TRPCError (FORBIDDEN or NOT_FOUND — pick what matches nearby patterns in the file/codebase). Note the frontend dropdown feeding this endpoint (apps/frontend/src/components/settings/sso-token-inspector.tsx) lists project members via `projectQueries.listProjectMembersWithRoles(ctx.project.id)`, so scoping to project members will not break the UI.

Keep the change minimal and in the style of the file. Do not touch other procedures.

There is a backend test file apps/backend/tests/auth-config-oidc.test.ts — read it, and if it covers inspectToken, add/adjust a test for the new scoping (target not in project → rejected; target in project → allowed). If it doesn't cover inspectToken at all, add a small test only if it fits the existing test structure easily; otherwise skip.

Verify: run `npm run -w @nao/backend test -- tests/auth-config-oidc.test.ts` (from repo root) if you touched tests, and check types compile for the file you edited (you can rely on the final repo-wide lint done later; do not run the full lint).

In your final response, state exactly what you changed and why, and paste any test results.

Fix two review issues from PR #1389, both in apps/backend/src/services/sso-group-mapping.service.ts. Read that file first, plus apps/backend/src/services/oidc-auth.service.ts, apps/backend/src/trpc/user.routes.ts (the `modify` mutation, ~lines 46-79) and apps/backend/tests/sso-group-mapping.test.ts.

ISSUE A (P2): `isGroupRoleMappingActive()` returns true whenever `OIDC_GROUP_ROLE_MAPPING` parses to a non-empty map and the SSO license feature is present — even when OIDC itself is not configured. Since `assertRolesAreEditable()` in apps/backend/src/trpc/trpc.ts blocks all manual role edits while the mapping is "active", a misconfigured deployment (mapping env set but no OIDC provider) leaves admins permanently unable to edit roles while no IdP sync can ever run. Fix: `isGroupRoleMappingActive()` must also require `isOidcConfigured()` (exported from './oidc-auth.service', already partially imported in the file via `getOidcProviderId`). Update/add tests in apps/backend/tests/sso-group-mapping.test.ts (and check apps/backend/tests/auth-config-oidc.test.ts still passes — it exercises `rolesManagedByIdp` via getConfig; note getConfig already returns null when OIDC is unconfigured, so behavior there should be unchanged, but the test mocks may need the oidc-auth.service mock adjusted).

ISSUE B (P2): In `applyRole()`, when the SSO sync demotes a project member out of `admin`/`context_admin` (via `projectQueries.updateProjectMemberRole`), it skips the context-explorer worktree cleanup that the manual demotion path performs. See apps/backend/src/trpc/user.routes.ts `modify`: after updating the role, if the project has a `path` and previousRole was 'admin' or 'context_admin' and the new role is neither, it calls `cleanupContextWorktree(projectId, project.path, userId)` from '../services/context-explorer-git.service'. Replicate that behavior in `applyRole` for each project demotion. You will need the project's `path` — either extend the query used (`projectQueries.listProjectMembershipsForUser`) to also return the project path (check apps/backend/src/queries/project.queries.ts; it currently selects only projectId and role from projectMember, so you'd join the project table), or fetch the project. Prefer extending the query with a join since it's one round-trip. IMPORTANT: check for import cycles — apps/backend/src/auth.ts imports this service, and elsewhere (auth.ts user.delete.before hook) `cleanupContextWorktree` is imported dynamically via `await import(...)` to avoid cycles; check whether a static import of context-explorer-git.service from this service file creates a cycle (context-explorer-git.service imports — read its imports). If in doubt, use the same dynamic-import pattern as auth.ts. Cleanup failures must not break the sync: the whole sync is already wrapped in try/catch that logs, but a cleanup failure for one project shouldn't abort role updates for the remaining projects — wrap the cleanup call itself in a try/catch that logs a warning (mirror the logging style used in the file with `logger.warn` and `serializeError`).

Add/adjust tests for both issues in apps/backend/tests/sso-group-mapping.test.ts following its existing mocking patterns.

Verify: run `npm run -w @nao/backend test -- tests/sso-group-mapping.test.ts tests/auth-config-oidc.test.ts` from the repo root and make them pass.

Fix three review issues from PR #1389, all in apps/frontend/src/components/auth-form.tsx. Read that file fully first, plus apps/frontend/src/components/auth-microsoft-button.tsx (for `useIsMicrosoftSetup`), apps/frontend/src/lib/last-sign-in-method.ts, and the AuthForm call sites: apps/frontend/src/routes/login.tsx, signup.tsx, forgot-password.tsx, reset-password.tsx, and apps/frontend/src/components/modify-password.tsx. Only login.tsx and signup.tsx pass `displaySocialProviders={true}`.

ISSUE 1 (P2, ~line 118): On a cold load of login/signup with a configured social provider, the provider setup queries (`isGoogleSetup`, `isGithubSetup`, `isGitlabSetup`, `useIsMicrosoftSetup`, `oidcConfig`) start as loading, so `socialProviders` is empty, `showsProviders` is false, and the email/password form renders expanded. When the queries resolve and a provider appears, the email form collapses — a visible flash and loss of focus if the user started typing. Fix by deferring the layout decision until the provider queries have settled: while `displaySocialProviders` is true and any of the provider queries is still pending, render neither the providers block nor the email form (the page header/logo can stay). Check what `useIsMicrosoftSetup` returns — if it only returns a boolean, read its implementation and extend it or use the underlying query so you can know its loading state; keep it clean. Once settled, current behavior applies. Make sure pages that do NOT display social providers (forgot/reset/modify password) are unaffected and never blocked on those queries.

ISSUE 2 (P3, ~line 159): The 'Last used' pill next to the collapsed 'Use email and password' button is dead code: when `lastSignInMethod === 'email'`, `isEmailFormExpanded` initializes to true so the collapsed button never renders. Remove the dead `{lastSignInMethod === 'email' && <LastUsedPill />}` conditional from that button (keep the button itself).

ISSUE 3 (P3, ~line 169): `emailLastUsed: lastSignInMethod === 'email'` is passed via CompactFieldsContext to all AuthForm consumers, so the 'Last used' pill shows on the email field of the forgot-password page (and any other non-sign-in page), mislabeling a password-reset form as a sign-in method. Fix by scoping the pill to actual sign-in/sign-up forms: only set `emailLastUsed` true when `displaySocialProviders` is true (that's exactly login/signup, and the pill is only meaningful when there are alternative methods to disambiguate).

Keep the diff minimal and match the file's existing style. After editing, check for linter errors in the file.

You are working in the repo /Users/blef/Work/naolabs/chat (a monorepo; frontend is apps/frontend: React, TanStack Query, Tailwind). Repo conventions: tabs for indentation, minimal comments, nao is lowercase.

Fix a P2 review issue from PR #1389 in apps/frontend/src/components/settings/sso-token-inspector.tsx (~line 30). Read the file first.

Problem: `selectedUserId` is plain useState. When the active project changes, the `members` query (`trpc.project.listAllUsersWithRoles`) refetches with the new project's members, but `selectedUserId` keeps pointing at a user from the previous project — so the inspector keeps showing (and the backend keeps being queried for) a user who is not a member of the current project. Note: the backend is being changed in parallel to reject inspection of users outside the current project, so a stale selection would now surface an error.

Fix: derive the effective userId so that a selection that is not present in the currently loaded `members` list falls back to the session user. Prefer a derived value over an effect, e.g.: keep `selectedUserId` state, but compute `const userId = members.data?.some((m) => m.id === selectedUserId) ? selectedUserId : session?.user?.id;` — take care not to reset the selection while `members` is still loading (when `members.data` is undefined, fall back to the previous behavior of `selectedUserId ?? session?.user?.id`, or just keep showing the session user; pick the cleanest behavior that avoids flicker and never inspects a non-member once data is loaded). Ensure the Select's `value` stays consistent with what's displayed.

Keep the diff minimal. After editing, check for linter errors in the file.

In your final response, state exactly what you changed and the behavior in each state (members loading / loaded with selection valid / loaded with selection stale).

You are working in the repo /Users/blef/Work/naolabs/chat (a monorepo; frontend is apps/frontend: React, TanStack Query/Form). Repo conventions: tabs for indentation, minimal comments, nao is lowercase.

Fix a P2 review issue from PR #1389 spanning apps/frontend/src/hooks/use-sso-role-mapping.ts and apps/frontend/src/components/settings/team/edit-member-dialog.tsx. Read both files fully first.

Problem: `useSsoRoleMapping()` returns `rolesManagedByIdp: data?.rolesManagedByIdp ?? false` — i.e. it reports "roles are editable" while the `trpc.authConfig.oidc.getConfig` query is still loading. `edit-member-dialog.tsx` uses this value to (a) enable/disable the role dropdown and (b) decide whether to send `newRole` on submit (`newRole: rolesManagedByIdp ? undefined : value.role`). During the loading window (cold cache / slow network) an admin on an IdP-managed deployment sees an enabled role editor; if they submit, the client sends `newRole` and the backend rejects with FORBIDDEN. 

Fix minimally: expose the query's loading state from the hook (e.g. return `isLoading` alongside `rolesManagedByIdp` and `providerName`), and in `edit-member-dialog.tsx` treat "still loading" as not-yet-editable: disable the role dropdown while loading (but do NOT show the "Roles are assigned from {providerName} groups..." helper text unless `rolesManagedByIdp` is actually true), and make the submit path safe — e.g. compute the disabled state from `rolesManagedByIdp || isLoading` for the dropdown. For the submit decision, `rolesManagedByIdp` will have resolved by the time a user actually submits in practice, but to be strict you can guard the submit the same way the dropdown is guarded (if the role can't be edited yet, send `newRole: undefined`). Do not treat unloaded config as "managed" for the helper-text/UI copy — only for the disabled state.

Check whether other components use `useSsoRoleMapping` (grep for it) and make sure your hook signature change doesn't break them; update them consistently if they have the same submit/disable pattern.

Keep the diff minimal. After editing, check for linter errors in the files you touched.

In your final response, state exactly what you changed in each file.

**Not fixing (4 issues):** multi-org scoping (the app assumes a single org membership everywhere), transactional role sync (matches the existing manual-path pattern), blocking login on the sync (deliberate, and largely mitigated by the OIDC-only gate), and click-time last-used recording (acceptable heuristic for a P3). Full rationale in the final report.

I'll verify with lint and the backend test suite once the agents finish.

todos.content: Run 6 GPT-5.6 subagents on the 9 accepted fixes

content.text:
All done. Of the 13 issues from the cubic review on [PR #1389](https://github.com/getnao/nao/pull/1389), I fixed 9 and rejected 4. Each fix was implemented by a GPT-5.6 subagent. Full lint passes; the OIDC/SSO test suites pass (44 + 13 tests, including new regression tests); the only failing backend tests are pre-existing environment failures that also fail without these changes. Nothing is committed yet.

## Fixed (9)

**1. P1 — `auth-config.routes.ts:99`: cross-tenant OIDC claims disclosure** — Valid, the most serious finding. Any project admin could read any user's stored ID-token claims by passing an arbitrary `userId`. `inspectToken` now allows self-inspection and otherwise requires the target to have a role in the caller's project, matching the member list the UI dropdown shows. Done by [Fix inspectToken cross-tenant leak](04b2f722-9035-40f2-94ab-3b7ce506028b), with tests for both the rejected and allowed cases.

**2. P2 — `trpc.ts:146`: role editing locked when OIDC is misconfigured** — Valid. Setting `OIDC_GROUP_ROLE_MAPPING` without a working OIDC provider would block all manual role edits forever while no sync could ever run. `isGroupRoleMappingActive()` now also requires `isOidcConfigured()`. Done by [Fix group-mapping service issues](39322aff-088e-4827-a6cd-35fa09f2db87).

**3. P2 — `sso-group-mapping.service.ts:162`: SSO demotions skip worktree cleanup** — Valid. The manual demotion path in `user.routes.ts` cleans up per-user context worktrees; the SSO sync didn't. `applyRole` now runs the same cleanup after each effective demotion out of `admin`/`context_admin`, with failures logged per-project so one bad worktree can't abort the rest of the sync. Same agent as #2, with regression tests.

**4. P2 — `auth.ts:323`: non-OIDC logins reapply stale OIDC groups** — Valid, and worth fixing given your `SSO_SESSION_MAX_AGE` commit exists precisely to force group refresh at re-login. The `session.create.after` hook now skips the sync unless the session was created by the OIDC callback (verified against better-auth's `/oauth2/callback/:providerId` route). Done by [Restrict role sync to OIDC sign-ins](faf97891-ea7f-4b99-a664-d161f6933be1).

**5. P2 — `auth-form.tsx:118`: email form flash on cold load** — Valid UX bug. The layout now waits for all five provider setup queries to settle before rendering either the provider buttons or the email form, so nothing collapses under the user's cursor. `useIsMicrosoftSetup` was extended to expose its pending state. Pages without social providers (forgot/reset password) are unaffected. Done by [Fix auth-form UI issues](d9d9d82b-8e7e-4f5f-a99b-147cbec13d56).

**6. P3 — `auth-form.tsx:159`: unreachable "Last used" pill** — Valid dead code; the collapsed email button can never coexist with `lastSignInMethod === 'email'`. Removed. Same agent as #5.

**7. P3 — `auth-form.tsx:169`: "Last used" badge on forgot-password** — Valid. `emailLastUsed` is now only set when `displaySocialProviders` is true, i.e. login/signup — which is also the only place the badge is meaningful. Same agent as #5.

**8. P2 — `sso-token-inspector.tsx:30`: stale user selection across project switch** — Valid, and made more visible by fix #1 (a stale selection would now hit a FORBIDDEN error). The effective user is now derived: once members are loaded, a selection not in the list falls back to the session user. Done by [Fix token inspector stale selection](e4659506-3bef-451a-b712-ce50db46b446).

**9. P2 — `use-sso-role-mapping.ts:5`: role editor enabled while config loads** — Valid. The hook now exposes `isLoading`, and the edit-member dialog disables the role dropdown and omits `newRole` while loading, so it can never send a role change the backend would reject. The "roles managed by your IdP" helper text still only shows when the mapping is actually active. Done by [Fix SSO role-mapping loading gap](554f5a8e-7fab-4edb-b5d8-24a143d58453).

## Not fixed (4)

**10. P2 — `sso-group-mapping.service.ts:150`: multi-org scoping** — Rejected. The entire codebase assumes one org membership per user: `getUserOrgMembership` selects with `limit 1`, and the org admin routes rely on the same single-membership model. The "unrelated organizations" scenario the review describes doesn't exist in the current data model; scoping the sync per-org would be speculative plumbing for a state the app can't reach.

**11. P2 — `sso-group-mapping.service.ts:157`: non-transactional sync, racy admin-count guard** — Rejected. The manual role-edit path (`user.routes.ts` `modify`) uses the exact same count-then-write pattern with no transaction, so the sync is consistent with the codebase's existing invariant handling. The race requires two of a project's last two admins being concurrently demoted by simultaneous SSO sign-ins — vanishingly narrow — and a cross-dialect (SQLite + Postgres) transactional rewrite isn't warranted for it.

**12. P3 — `auth.ts:322`: sync blocks the login response** — Rejected as stated, though fix #4 removes the cost for every non-OIDC sign-in. For OIDC sign-ins, awaiting the sync is deliberate: a demoted user should get their reduced role before their first authenticated request, and the cost is a handful of small queries once per sign-in. Fire-and-forget would trade correctness for negligible latency.

**13. P3 — `auth-form.tsx:68`: last-used recorded on click, not on success** — Rejected. Recording on click is the standard heuristic for "last used" hints; recording on success would require threading state through the OAuth callback for a purely cosmetic hint whose worst failure is one wrong pill after a cancelled OAuth attempt.

One caveat on my verification: fixes #5–#9 are visual behaviors I verified by code reading and lint only — worth a quick manual pass on the login page and the team settings dialog before you push.
